name: mossy dry-stone retaining wall segment (Japanese countryside, chains horizontally)
label: jp_inaka_pack/inaka-mossy-stone-wall
reasons: 화풍: 칸 정보량이 기준보다 훨씬 낮음 (1/4)

answer.evidence: Rows 5-11 form a 7-row moss-covered top band with a ragged lower edge. A dark moss edge line sits at row 12 (L=75 at x=16 and x=47, and a dark drip at x=32 down to row 16), which acts as an eave shadow. Below it, rows 13-29 show a vertical stone face of about 17 rows, with horizontal joints at rows 15-16 and 22-23 and vertical mortar gaps. The base is dark at row 30. The wall has no receding side face and the silhouette is a uniform 64 px wide. The top band is a real horizontal surface, not just a rim, so this is a three-quarter view.

styleAnswer.evidence: The references are whole houses (roof, walls, door, windows). The candidate is a low wall strip with a mossy top and about three grey stone courses. I can't match the kind, but the stone and moss material can still be compared to the stone wall on house-h112_0-stone. Distinct colours are 13, against 66 and 185 for the references, so the palette is far narrower. The median of 12 colours per tile is close to h112's 11, but that is partly because the piece is thin. Each stone has only about 2-3 grey steps (light top edge, mid face, dark joint) where the reference stones have 5-6, with per-stone highlights and tinted shadows. The moss has only 2-3 greens and some tuft dots on top, and the grass tufts are sparse. Dark edge pixels are 22% neutral against 7-9% for the references, so the outline leans grey and is only partly tinted. The stone joints are cool dark grey with little warm or green tint. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat areas. Overall it is readable but shallower and more uniform than the references, with fewer colours and less per-stone variation. When in doubt, fail.

styleAnswer.evidence: The references are whole buildings with roof, walls and door, while the candidate is a low wall segment. The kind does not match, so I judged it by eye against the stone wall of house-h112_0-stone. But it has only 13 distinct colours in total against 66 and 185 for the references, so its ramps are shallow. The grey stone blocks and the moss strip carry about 3-4 lightness steps each, not the 5-6 the references use. 22% of its dark edge pixels are neutral against 7-9% for the references, so the outlines lean toward grey-black and look somewhat sticker-like. Compared with the richly shaded stone-and-tile wall in the reference it looks flatter and thinner. When in doubt, fail.

styleAnswer.evidence: The references are whole houses (roof, walls, door), while the candidate is a low wall strip, so the kind match is only partial. The closest comparison is the stone wall of h112. The candidate has only 13 distinct colours against 66 and 185 for the references, so its ramps are shallow. The grey stone has about 3 steps and the moss about 3 greens, against roughly 5-6 steps per material in Beodeul. Its per-tile median of 12 colours is on par with h112 (11), and flat-fill coverage is 0%. That density comes from a small palette dithered in a repeating block pattern, not from graded shading. That is more neutral than the references but not a pure black sticker outline, so I call it mixed.
